ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of $\odot O$, point C is the midpoint of $\overset{\frown}{BD}$, CF is a chord of $\odot O$, and CF $\perp$ AB with the foot of the perpendicular at point E. Connect BD and CF at point G, and connect CD, AD, BF. $\triangle BFG \cong \triangle CDG$; if AD=10 and EF=15, find the length of BE.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line OF,\\
$\because$ arc CD = arc CB = arc BF,\\
$\therefore$ arc CF = arc DB,\\
$\therefore$ BD = CF = 2, EF = 30,\\
$\because$ AD = 10, $\angle ADB = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ AB = $10\sqrt{10}$,\\
$\therefore$ OF = $5\sqrt{10}$,\\
$\because$ CF $\perp$ AB,\\
$\therefore$ OE = 5, BE = $5\sqrt{10} - 5 = \boxed{5\sqrt{10} - 5}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, AB is the horizontal diameter, A is at the left end, B is at the right end, and O is on AB as the center of the circle. The vertical chord CF is located on the right side of the circle, C is above, F is below, CF is perpendicular to AB, the intersection point is E, and from the figure it can be seen that E is between O and B. Point D is at the upper left of the circle, and AD, CD, BD, and BF are connected; BD and CF intersect at G. Reasoning: From the problem statement and the figure, G is the intersection point of BD and CF, and △BFG ≅ △CDG, so the corresponding sides BF = CD. Also because C is the midpoint of arc BD, arc BC = arc CD. Equal chords correspond to equal arcs; from BF = CD, arc BF = arc CD, so arc BF, arc BC, and arc CD are equal. Thus the minor arc CF passing through B = arc CB + arc BF, while arc DB = arc DC + arc CB; the two are equal, so the corresponding chords CF = BD. Because AB passes through the center O and is perpendicular to chord CF at E, when a diameter is perpendicular to a chord, it bisects the chord, so CE = EF. Given EF = 15, so CF = 2EF = 30, therefore BD = 30. AB is a diameter, so ∠ADB = 90°. In right triangle ADB, AD = 10, BD = 30, therefore AB = sqrt(AD^2 + BD^2) = sqrt(10^2 + 30^2) = sqrt(1000) = 10√10. The radius of the circle OB = OF = AB/2 = 5√10. In right triangle OEF, OF^2 = OE^2 + EF^2, so OE = sqrt((5√10)^2 - 15^2) = sqrt(250 - 225) = 5. From the figure it can be seen that E is between O and B, therefore BE = OB - OE = 5√10 - 5.
